prompt:
Build an Android hospital appointment booking app in Java.

Features:

- Settings screen to enter and save the Gemini API key.
- Separate Settings field for the default AI system instruction/niche prompt.
- AI acts as a Hospital Appointment Assistant.
- User can type or speak; AI responds with text and voice.
- Add attractive AI animations for listening, thinking, and speaking.
- AI collects patient name, age, phone, department, doctor, date, and time.
- Maintain a structured appointment metadata/state containing all collected information.
- Save the latest metadata locally and send it with every Gemini request.
- Use previous metadata for follow-up questions and never ask again for information already collected.
- Update only changed/missing metadata fields.
- Before booking, show a complete appointment summary and ask for confirmation.
- Only after clear user confirmation, send the validated appointment data to the PHP/MySQL backend.
- Insert the confirmed appointment into SQL/MySQL using a secure API and prepared statements.
- Never tell the user an appointment is confirmed until the backend successfully returns a booking confirmation.
- Add an Admin screen to view all booked appointments from the database.
- Clean modern hospital + AI UI with loading states, error handling, microphone permissions, and secure API/database handling.
- Never expose MySQL credentials inside the Android app.
- Handle Gemini/API, network, speech recognition, JSON parsing, and database errors gracefully.
Look at the build errors and fix them.

Modify the existing Android hospital appointment app.

IMPORTANT:

- Remove MySQL, PHP backend, remote SQL APIs, database credentials, and all server-side database code.
- Use ONLY Android SQLite for appointment storage.
- Use Gemini 2.5 Flash as the Gemini AI model.

Requirements:

- Use "SQLiteOpenHelper" or "SQLiteDatabase" in Java.
- Create a local "appointments" table.
- Store patient name, age, phone, department, doctor, date, time, status, and created_at.
- After the user confirms an appointment, insert the validated appointment directly into SQLite using Java.
- Use parameterized/prepared SQLite queries.
- Do not send appointment data to MySQL or PHP.
- Admin screen must read appointments directly from the local SQLite database.
- Add appointment search, details, and status management.
- Keep the existing Gemini API integration, using Gemini 2.5 Flash.
- Keep metadata/state management and send the latest appointment metadata with every Gemini request.
- Maintain conversation context for follow-up questions and never ask again for information already collected.
- Keep voice input, voice output, AI animations, API-key Settings, and separate default AI instruction Settings unchanged.
- Never claim an appointment is confirmed until the SQLite INSERT succeeds.
- Remove all unused MySQL/PHP-related code and dependencies.
- Do not hardcode the Gemini API key.
- Handle Gemini errors, invalid JSON, SQLite errors, network errors, and speech errors gracefully.
- Ensure the final Android project compiles successfully with no missing classes, resources, imports, or dependencies.
